reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset and Brown restrict the extermination command to incorrigibly wicked Canaanite nations under judicial sentence, unlike the loved stranger.

discrepancy.note: Paine indicts the Canaanite extermination order as one of the indiscriminate, morally monstrous slaughters this same God is said to command.

quotes.text: the indiscriminate judgements upon men, women and children, with which this lying book, the bible, is crowded; such as Noah's flood, the destruction of the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, the extirpation of the Canaanites, even to suckling infants, and women with child
quotes.attr: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason, Part II (1795), ch. I, on Deuteronomy 7:2.

sides.snippet: you shall love him as yourself; for you lived as foreigners in the land of Egypt
sides.verseText: The stranger who lives as a foreigner with you shall be to you as the native-born among you, and you shall love him as yourself; for you lived as foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am Yahweh your God.

sides.snippet: then you shall utterly destroy them: you shall make no covenant with them, nor show mercy to them;
sides.verseText: and when Yahweh your God shall deliver them up before you, and you shall strike them; then you shall utterly destroy them: you shall make no covenant with them, nor show mercy to them;
